candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record documents autonomic dysfunction (abnormal cardiac parasympathetic function, anhidrosis on TST/QSART) as one feature, but the benchmark diagnosis is Pseudo-α-galactosidase deficiency (PAGD) syndrome with mild neurocognitive disorder — a specific genetic/enzymatic entity confirmed by reduced α-galactosidase activity, positive pseudo-α-galactosidase allele, pulvinar MRI signal, and neurocognitive deficits. 'Autonomic nervous system dysfunction, global' names only a manifestation/component and omits the etiologic diagnosis and the neurocognitive component.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Autonomic nervous system dysfunction is a prominent component of the clinical presentation but does not capture the specific etiology (pseudo-α-galactosidase deficiency), the genetic basis, the neurocognitive disorder component, or the full composite diagnostic object

case_quality_flags: PAGD is an extremely rare and recently described entity; the CSF differential (83% lymphocytes, elevated protein) and pulvinar hyperintensity are atypical features that may complicate differential diagnosis
Reduced α-galactosidase activity with pseudo-allele positivity is the key distinguishing finding from classic Fabry disease
